newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Siebe H1 profits seen up 25 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Siebe H1 profits seen up 25 pct.

text.p: Investors will be expecting another robust performance from diversified engineering group Siebe Plc when it reports first-half results next Tuesday, with headline pretax profits boosted by its acquisition of the 500-million stg electronic power controls company Unitech.

Analysts are forecasting pretax profits for the six months to September 30 to jump to around 182 million stg from 144.2 million stg last time, with a 10 percent rise in the interim dividend to 4.89 pence on earnings up 20 percent at 23 pence.
Up 7-1/2p at 952-1/2 on Friday, Siebe's share price has jumped 24 percent in the last 12 months, from 768 pence, keeping the stock on a characteristically high rating.
According to Reuters 3000 data it has outperformed the London FTSE all-share index by 11.8 percent in the last 12 months and the FTSE engineering index by 1.8 percent.

The current share price puts Siebe at a 6.43 percent premium to the sector, pricing it at 18.53 times forecast earnings, according to market estimates data supplied to Reuters 3000 by Edinburgh Financial.

But the data shows the market expects earnings to jump a further 20 percent to around 60.2 pence a share next year from around 52 pence in 1996/97, putting Siebe on a more modest forward multiple of 15.7 times.

Last year's pre-tax profits jumped 20.4 percent to 331.1 million stg, topping analysts' forecasts of around 325 million, and the company has vowed to grow profits by at least 15 percent this year before acquisitions, on a 10 percent rise in sales.
Analysts are looking for full-year pretax profits to rise to 430 million stg this year and 500 million stg next year.
